assessments.rationale: Manufacturing bio-based composites instead of fossil-based plastics reduces the environmental footprint (m) and carbon footprint of production (Page 33, Page 80). It also addresses and minimizes the release of microplastics and nanoplastics (p) during manufacturing processes like cutting and molding, aligning with the zero-pollution ambition (Page 3, Page 7, Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: May conflict with the Use phase and End-of-Life phase, as bio-based composites can have lower durability (Page 33) and are more difficult to recycle compared to standard plastics.

assessments.rationale: Snap-fits eliminate the need for adhesives or additional metal fasteners, which minimizes the consumption of resources in production (g) and reduces the amount of waste generated in production (r) by avoiding scrap and consumable waste (Page 7, Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with repairability (Page 33) and End-of-Life phases, as snap-fits can easily break during disassembly, preventing successful repair, maintenance, or reuse.

assessments.rationale: Brushed AC motors have a simpler manufacturing process compared to brushless DC motors, which require high-energy processing and rare-earth magnets. This reduces the consumption of energy and resources in production (g) and lowers the overall environmental/carbon footprint of manufacturing (m) (Page 3, Page 81).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use phase, as brushed motors are less energy-efficient (Page 3, Page 33) and have a shorter lifespan, which increases the user's energy footprint and vulnerability to energy price increases.

assessments.rationale: Passive cooling heatsinks require fewer manufacturing steps and no complex electronic or fluid assembly, minimizing energy and water consumption in production (g) and preventing the generation of hazardous waste (r) associated with coolant fluids or active fan components (Page 80, Page 33).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use phase, as passive cooling may limit the motor's power density and thermal efficiency, potentially reducing the functional performance and energy efficiency of the vacuum cleaner (Page 33, Page 80).

assessments.rationale: A monolithic integrated design simplifies the manufacturing line, reducing assembly energy, resource consumption (g), and production-line waste (r). It also minimizes emissions to air, water, and soil (q) by reducing the number of processing steps and tooling requirements (Page 3, Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Directly conflicts with the Repairability and Circularity phases, as monolithic designs make repair, maintenance, refurbishment, and material recovery extremely difficult or impossible (Page 33).

assessments.rationale: Corded AC power completely avoids the highly resource-intensive, high-emission, and hazardous waste-generating processes of manufacturing lithium-ion battery cells, thereby drastically reducing the environmental footprint (m), emissions to air, water, and soil (q), and hazardous waste generation (r) in production (Page 3, Page 80).
assessments.potential_conflicts_with: Conflicts with the Use phase (user convenience and portability) and potentially End-of-Life phase if the cord contains copper and PVC that must be managed, though battery waste is far more hazardous.
